rules.title: Prohibition on sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms (BMC 13.63)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license, or provide to Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential units in Berkeley, and unlawful for a landlord to use such an algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels. Each month of violation and each unit for which the algorithm was used is a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation

coverage_conditions.summary: All residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley and landlords/vendors providing coordinated pricing algorithms using non-public competitor data less than 90 days old.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Applies to algorithms using non-public Competitor Data (less than 90 days old) to recommend rents, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms in coordination between a landlord and competitors, including through third-party vendors.

rules.exemptions: Excludes products that publish aggregated, anonymous rental data without recommending rents or terms; products used to set rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines; products used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing or training for software development.
rules.interaction: Does not regulate the amount of rent a landlord may charge; does not prevent development or sale of software using public data or general property management software.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Berkeley Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers may not inquire about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decisions, including refusing to rent or terminate a tenancy, requiring disclosure, demanding higher deposits or rent, or refusing to add a family member based on criminal history.

coverage_conditions.summary: Rental housing providers in Berkeley, except owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where the owner resides, and other listed exemptions.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Exempt if an owner of record resides in one of the units (1-3 unit property) as primary residence.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Exempt: lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; units under rental agreements allowing owners to move back (BMC 13.76.130 A.9); units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.

rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; public housing/Section 8 properties (limited exemptions); owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record resides as primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.interaction: Supersedes r-0003 (Fair Chance written notice and opportunity to respond): R1 states it has the same coverage and exemptions as the Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (R2), so R1's notice-and-response duty operates within R2's scope and exemptions.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

rules.title: Fair Chance written notice and opportunity to respond
rules.requirement: If a landlord takes any action against an applicant or tenant based on criminal history, the landlord must give the applicant or tenant written notice and an opportunity to respond.

coverage_conditions.summary: Same coverage as the Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance, net of its exemptions.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Exempt if owner-occupied 1-3 unit property where an owner of record resides.

rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as the ordinance generally (lifetime sex offenders, limited public housing/Section 8, owner-occupied 1-3 units, owner move-back agreements, sublet/roommate changes).
rules.interaction: Yields to r-0002 (Berkeley Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance): R1 states it has the same coverage and exemptions as the Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (R2), so R1's notice-and-response duty operates within R2's scope and exemptions.
rules.quoted_span: If a landlord takes any action against an applicant or tenant based on criminal history (such as refusing to offer a lease, refusing to add a family member, etc.), the landlord is required to provide the applicant/tenant with written notice and an opportunity to respond.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for owner move-in and Ellis Act evictions (2026 adjustment)
rules.requirement: Owners must pay tenants relocation assistance when evicting for an owner move-in or to remove a property from the rental market under the Ellis Act. The payments are indexed annually to inflation and the Rent Board publishes the yearly increase.
rules.key_value: Standard payment $19,413; additional payment for qualifying households $6,471 (effective January 1, 2026)

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenants evicted for owner move-in or Ellis Act withdrawal of the property from the rental market; the document does not state further coverage limits.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Applies to owner move-in evictions and Ellis Act evictions; the additional payment applies to qualifying households.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance; Ellis Implementation Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance requires owners to pay tenants relocation assistance in the event of an owner move-in eviction.

rules.title: Prohibition of non-refundable application fees for existing tenancies (BMC 13.78.016)
rules.requirement: An owner or the owner's agent may not charge any existing tenant a non-refundable fee for renewing a tenancy, including fees tied to a roommate's departure or a request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

coverage_conditions.summary: Owners of residential rental property and their agents, as to existing tenants.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Applies to existing tenants renewing a tenancy or changing roommates.

rules.interaction: BMC 13.78.018 provides that Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements despite contrary lease terms.
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

rules.title: Tenant screening fee rights disclosure and fee cap statement (BMC 13.78.010)
rules.requirement: When an owner charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report or process an application, the owner must provide, in the rental application or a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b).
rules.key_value: Maximum tenant screening fee for 2026: $68.96

coverage_conditions.summary: Owners or agents who charge a fee to purchase a consumer credit report or to validate, review or process a rental application in Berkeley.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Applies when the owner charges a screening or application processing fee.

rules.interaction: Implements and notifies applicants of the state limit under California Civil Code Section 1950.6.

rules.title: State tenant screening fee limits (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6)
rules.requirement: Screening fees are capped (2026 maximum $68.96). Landlords may not charge a screening fee if no unit is available, must provide a copy of the credit report, a receipt, an itemized list of expenses and a refund of any unused portion, and must accept a reusable screening report if the tenant provides one. A fee must be returned to applicants not selected unless the landlord reviews applications in order received and does not charge applicants not considered.
rules.key_value: $68.96 maximum for 2026

coverage_conditions.summary: Landlords charging screening fees to prospective tenants.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Applies to prospective tenants charged a screening fee.

rules.interaction: Berkeley BMC 13.78.010 requires disclosure of this state cap.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available.
rules.conflict_note: Conflict among r-0007, r-0050: Both describe the Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6 screening fee cap but state different figures: R3 gives a 2026 maximum of $68.96, while R6 gives $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted annually. These are probably consistent, since $68.96 would be the CPI-adjusted 2026 amount of the $30 base. A reviewer should confirm this and treat them as one rule from two sources rather than two caps.

rules.title: Annual General Adjustment capped at 5% (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: The Annual General Adjustment (AGA), the yearly amount by which landlords of fully covered units may raise rent, is set by a CPI-based formula but may not exceed 5%. Landlords with banked AGAs may still raise rent above 5% to reach the rent ceiling.
rules.key_value: Maximum AGA of 5%

coverage_conditions.summary: Fully covered rental units under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Applies to fully covered units, not partially covered or exempt units.

rules.exemptions: Cap does not prevent a landlord with banked (unused) AGAs from raising rent by more than 5% to reach the rent ceiling.
rules.interaction: Supersedes r-0039 (Statewide rent cap (Civ. Code § 1947.12, as amended by SB 567)): R7's exemptions and coverage_conditions exclude housing under stricter local rent control, and Berkeley's AGA cap of 5% is below the state cap of 5% plus CPI (up to 10%) for fully covered units.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

rules.title: Government-owned or -subsidized units brought under rent ceiling (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: Landlords of government-owned or -subsidized units must register them as fully or partially covered. Fully covered units have a rent ceiling, with increases limited by the Annual General Adjustment.
rules.key_value: Rent increases limited by the Annual General Adjustment

coverage_conditions.summary: Government-owned or -subsidized units (Section 8, Shelter Plus Care, VASH, LIHTC, HOME and others) that are fully covered, such as most units in multifamily properties built before 1980. Units are partially covered where federal or state law or regulation prohibits rent control.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Coverage depends on unit type and on whether federal law, state law or administrative regulation exempts the unit from rent control.

rules.exemptions: Section 202 and Section 811 units, and certain HUD-insured or HUD-held projects, are only partially covered because other law prohibits rent control.
rules.interaction: Federal law, state law or administrative regulation that prohibits rent control limits coverage to partial for some subsidized units.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: Units that are fully covered will have a rent ceiling, meaning rent increases will be limited by the

rules.title: Capital improvement rent petitions limited to completed work (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: Landlords may petition for rent increases only for completed capital improvements, not for planned ones.

coverage_conditions.summary: Landlords of units covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance who petition for rent increases.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: Landlords can only file a petition for rent increases for completed capital improvements (they can no longer petition to have rent increases preliminarily authorized for planned capital improvements).

rules.title: Utility charges must be in base rent or separately metered (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: For tenancies starting on or after February 6, 2024, a landlord may charge a tenant in a fully covered unit for utilities only if the cost is part of the base rent, or the utility is separately metered and the lease requires the tenant to put the account in the tenant's name. Landlords charging separately may petition to add the average utility cost to the rent ceiling.

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenants in fully covered units with tenancies starting on or after February 6, 2024.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Fully covered units only.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies starting on or after February 6, 2024, a landlord may charge a tenant in a fully covered unit for utilities only if either: the cost of the  utilities are part of the base rent, or the utility service is separately-metered and the lease requires the tenant to place the utility in the tenant’s name.

rules.title: Just cause required for eviction (Berkeley Rent Ordinance)
rules.requirement: Tenants in units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted without just cause. Measure BB changed some just causes and eliminated one.

coverage_conditions.summary: Fully or partially covered units. A unit where the tenant shares a kitchen or bath with the landlord is exempt only if the landlord lived on the same property at the start of the tenancy.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Shared-facility exemption applies only if the landlord resided on the property at the start of the tenancy.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Exempt units are outside the requirement.

rules.exemptions: Exempt units, including shared kitchen or bath units where the landlord lived on the property before the tenant.
rules.interaction: Supersedes r-0036 (Statewide just cause eviction (Tenant Protection Act, Civ. Code § 1946.2)): R9's interaction field says it does not apply where a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019 applies, and the Berkeley ordinance covers the same tenancies.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)

rules.title: Nonpayment eviction requires debt of at least one month's Fair Market Rent (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict for nonpayment of rent only if the tenant owes at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent for a unit of equivalent size.
rules.key_value: Rental debt of at least one month's HUD Fair Market Rent (Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR)

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenants in fully or partially covered units.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.

rules.title: No eviction for refusing to sign a new lease (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease when a fixed-term lease expires.

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenants in fully or partially covered units with fixed-term leases.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Applies upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.

rules.title: Lease-violation evictions require material, harmful, unreasonable breach (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: To evict for violating a material lease term, the term must be mutually agreed, the violation must cause substantial actual damage to the landlord, and the tenant's behavior must be unreasonable. The notice to stop the violation must specify the term and describe the violation and harm in enough detail for a reasonable person to understand.

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenants in fully or partially covered units.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: The landlord’s notice to the tenant to stop the violation (which is required before the landlord can serve an eviction notice) must specify the lease term, and describe the violation and resulting harm in enough detail for a reasonable person to understand.

rules.title: Eviction notices and lawsuits must be filed with Rent Board within 3 business days (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: Landlords must file with the Rent Board a copy of any termination notice, notice to quit, and summons and complaint within three business days of serving the tenant. Termination notices must also state that advice is available from the Rent Board and give its counseling phone number and website.
rules.key_value: 3 business days

coverage_conditions.summary: Landlords of fully or partially covered units terminating a tenancy.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: The landlord must file with the Rent Board a copy of any notice to terminate a tenancy, notice to quit, and summons and complaint no later than three business days after the tenant was served with the document.

rules.title: Annual inflation adjustment of owner move-in relocation payments (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: The Rent Board must make inflationary adjustments each year to the relocation assistance amounts paid for owner move-in evictions.
rules.key_value: Mandatory yearly inflationary adjustment

coverage_conditions.summary: Owner move-in evictions in units covered by the Rent Ordinance.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: The Rent Board must make inflationary adjustments to owner move-in eviction relocation assistance amounts each year.

rules.title: Security deposit cap (AB 12)
rules.requirement: Starting July 1, 2024, landlords may charge no more than one month's rent as a security deposit, for furnished and unfurnished units. Small landlords may charge up to two months' rent. Last month's rent counts toward the deposit and first month's rent does not.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords)

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential tenancies in California. Small landlords with two rental properties and no more than four units total may charge up to two months' rent.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: The two-month cap applies to landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total, where ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or LLC whose members are all natural persons.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Applies to both furnished and unfurnished units. Last month's rent is part of the deposit; first month's rent is not.

rules.exemptions: Small landlords (two properties, no more than four units total, owned by a natural person, family trust, or all-natural-person LLC) may charge up to two months' rent.
rules.interaction: State law applied in Berkeley. The Rent Board says it cannot determine whether a landlord may charge one or two months' rent for a new tenancy.
rules.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units
rules.conflict_note: Conflict among r-0018, r-0041: R6 says a small landlord may charge up to two months' rent and does not mention R11's service-member exception, where the one-month cap applies. R6's interaction field also says the Berkeley Rent Board cannot determine whether a landlord may charge one or two months' rent for a new tenancy. A reviewer should confirm the service-member carve-out applies and how the cap is applied in Berkeley.

rules.title: Permitted security deposit deductions
rules.requirement: A landlord may deduct only the amount reasonably necessary to cover rent default, repair tenant-caused damage beyond normal wear and tear, clean the unit to its move-in condition, and, if the lease allows, restore or replace personal property or furniture. A landlord may not charge for professional cleaning unless reasonably necessary to restore move-in condition.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential tenancies in California. Cleaning deductions apply to tenancies beginning after January 1, 2003.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Cleaning deduction applies to tenancies beginning after January 1, 2003. Personal property or furniture deductions require lease authorization.

rules.citation: California state law (section not cited in document)
rules.quoted_span: A landlord may deduct only the amount that is reasonably necessary to:

rules.title: Security deposit return within 21 days with itemized statement
rules.requirement: The landlord must return all or any remaining portion of the deposit within 21 days after the tenant vacates. If deductions are made, the landlord must give a written itemized statement with copies of bills, invoices or receipts for repair and cleaning charges.
rules.key_value: 21 days

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential tenancies in California.

rules.citation: California state law (section not cited in document)

rules.title: Post-move-out photographs and proof of repairs for deductions
rules.requirement: Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must photograph the unit after regaining possession and before any repairs or cleaning for which they intend to deduct from the deposit. They must give the tenant the photos and a written explanation of costs with the itemized statement. Starting January 1, 2025, landlords must also provide proof that necessary repairs were completed.

coverage_conditions.summary: Landlords making security deposit deductions for repair or cleaning in California.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Applies when the landlord intends to make deductions for repairs or cleaning.

rules.citation: California state law (section not cited in document)
rules.quoted_span: Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must take photographs of a unit after regaining possession, but before any repairs or cleaning for which the landlord intends to make a deduction from the security deposit.

rules.title: Pre-tenancy unit photographs
rules.requirement: For tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy to document its condition.

coverage_conditions.summary: New tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025.

rules.quoted_span: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy to document the condition of the unit.

rules.title: Move-out walk-through inspection
rules.requirement: Landlords must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of a tenancy so the tenant can correct repair or cleaning items and avoid deposit deductions.
rules.key_value: Last two weeks of tenancy

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential tenancies in California.

rules.citation: California state law (section not cited in document)
rules.quoted_span: Under state law, landlords must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of a tenancy to identify any items that need repair/cleaning.

rules.title: Berkeley security deposit interest requirement
rules.requirement: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on the security deposit at the end of each year. They must pay a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before year-end.
rules.key_value: Annual interest, prorated on move-out

coverage_conditions.summary: Units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Unit must be fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (section not cited in document)
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

rules.title: Berkeley 2026 Annual General Adjustment (Regulation 1148)
rules.requirement: Eligible landlords may increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026. The AGA is set at 65% of the Bay Area CPI-U increase for July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025.
rules.key_value: 1.0% (65% of 1.5% Bay Area CPI)

coverage_conditions.summary: Rent-stabilized Berkeley units whose landlords are eligible under Regulation 1148; the AGA may not adjust rents for tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 whose rents were set under Costa-Hawkins.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Excludes tenancies beginning on or after January 1, 2025 with rents set pursuant to the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act. Landlords must meet the conditions and give the notice set out in Regulation 1148.

rules.exemptions: Tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 and had their rents set pursuant to the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act are not adjusted by the 2026 AGA.
rules.interaction: Interacts with the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act, which governs initial rents for certain tenancies. Supersedes r-0039 (Statewide rent cap (Civ. Code § 1947.12, as amended by SB 567)): R7 exempts housing under stricter local rent control, and Berkeley's 2026 AGA of 1.0% is stricter than the state cap for eligible rent-stabilized units.

rules.quoted_span:
adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow

rules.requirement: Rent control applies to fully covered units: most multifamily units built before 1980, single-family homes with tenancies that began before 1996, and rooming houses. Partially covered and exempt units are not subject to rent control.

coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Single-family homes covered only if the current tenancy began before 1996. Not rent controlled: new construction with certificate of occupancy after June 1980, single-family tenancies beginning on or after Jan 1, 1996, most condominiums, and certain federally subsidized units.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy – criminal history
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers may not impose a blanket denial of housing based on arrests or convictions and must assess applicants case by case. They may not consider non-conviction arrests, convictions subject to judicial relief, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old when determining eligibility or considering eviction.
rules.key_value: No blanket bans; excludes arrests without conviction, judicially relieved convictions, juvenile records, and convictions over 5 years old

rules.title: Rental assistance (source of income) discrimination prohibited in Boston housing
rules.requirement: Landlords in Boston may not discriminate against renters based on their use of rental assistance. Refusing to accept Section 8, social security disability, or veterans vouchers is cited as an example of housing discrimination.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to renting, buying, selling, or financing housing in the City of Boston. The page states no exemptions.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Protects renters using rental assistance such as Section 8 vouchers, social security disability vouchers, and veterans vouchers.

rules.interaction: Enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission alongside local, state, and federal fair housing laws.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Housing Regulations (Boston.gov, Fair Housing and Equity); no section number given
rules.quoted_span: The landlord tells you they don't accept rental assistance.

rules.title: Source of income discrimination ban (FEHA)
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not refuse to rent to, or apply different terms to, applicants or tenants based on source of income, including Section 8 vouchers and other rental assistance. They must also comply with the paperwork and inspection requirements of subsidy programs.

coverage_conditions.summary: Most housing accommodations in California, including landlords, property managers and tenant screening companies.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: An owner occupying the home and renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics, per the document's general FEHA FAQ.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied home renting to one additional person (per the general FEHA exclusion described); housing specifically for seniors may be limited by age.
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: Refusing to rent to a tenant with a section 8 voucher.

rules.title: Criminal history screening limits (FEHA)
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not consider arrests that did not lead to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile justice records, and may not impose blanket bans on applicants with a criminal history. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to the applicant's ability to be a good tenant and not a threat to the health and safety of others or the property.

coverage_conditions.summary: Housing providers and tenant screening companies covered by FEHA, for most housing in California.

rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system.

rules.title: Ban on common pricing algorithm used in anticompetitive combination (AB 325, B&P Code § 16729(a))
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of the Cartwright Act. A common pricing algorithm is any methodology used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set, or otherwise influence a price or commercial term.

coverage_conditions.summary: General antitrust rule covering any person (not the end consumer) who uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm, including software used to set rents. It is not limited to housing.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Applies to any 'person' as defined in Section 16702, excluding the end consumer. The algorithm must be used by two or more persons and use competitor data.

rules.interaction: Does not impair or limit the applicability of other antitrust laws (Cartwright Act provisions).
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.

rules.title: Ban on coercing adoption of common pricing algorithm recommendations (AB 325, B&P Code § 16729(b))
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt the price or commercial term the algorithm recommends for the same or similar products or services in California.

coverage_conditions.summary: General rule covering any person who uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm and coerces others to adopt its recommended prices or commercial terms. It is not limited to housing, but can reach rental pricing software.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Requires coercion of another person to adopt the recommended price or commercial term.

rules.interaction: Does not impair or limit the applicability of other antitrust laws.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.

rules.title: Statewide just cause eviction (Tenant Protection Act, Civ. Code § 1946.2)
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months, the owner may not terminate the tenancy without a just cause stated in the written termination notice. Just cause is either at-fault (e.g. nonpayment, breach, nuisance) or no-fault (e.g. owner move-in, withdrawal from rental market, government order, demolition or substantial remodel).
rules.key_value: 12 months of occupancy (24 months if adult tenants were added to the lease before 24 months and not all tenants have 12 months)

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential tenancies of 12+ months, except housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years, qualifying owner-occupied or single-family properties with non-corporate owners who gave the required notice, dormitories, transient hotels, certain care facilities, deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing, and properties covered by a local just cause ordinance.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Exempt: a separately alienable single-family residence or mobilehome whose owner is not a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member, if the tenants received the required written exemption notice. Also exempt: owner-occupied residences renting no more than two units or bedrooms, and owner-occupied duplexes.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Does not apply to mobilehome homeowners. Does not apply to housing restricted as affordable or subsidized for very low, low or moderate income households.  Tenancy must be continuous and lawful for 12 months.  Waiver of rights is void.  Owner failure to comply voids the termination notice.  Section is repealed January 1, 2030.  Housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years is exempt unless it is a mobilehome.  Exemptions also cover transient and tourist hotels, nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, adult residential facilities, and school or institutional dormitories.  Single-family owner-occupied residences and mobilehomes are also exempt.  Housing with a shared bathroom or kitchen where the owner lives on the property is exempt.  A two-unit property where the owner occupies one unit at the start of the tenancy and continues to occupy it is exempt, unless a unit is an ADU or JADU.  Properties with qualifying exempt owner status must give written notice of the exemption in the rental agreement for tenancies commenced or renewed on or after July 1, 2020 (July 1, 2022 for mobilehomes).  Residential real property that is alienable separate from title to any other dwelling unit is exempt only if the owner is not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member (or mobilehome park management) and the notice requirements are met.  Housing deed-restricted as affordable is exempt.  Local ordinances adopted on or before September 1, 2019, and more protective later ordinances, apply instead.  The section is operative April 1, 2024.

rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotels; nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care and licensed residential care facilities; school and higher-education dormitories; shared-facility housing with an owner-occupant; single-family owner-occupied residences (up to two units or bedrooms rented) and mobilehomes; owner-occupied duplexes; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); separately alienable residential property whose owner is not a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member and who gave the required notice; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; mobilehome homeowners; property subject to a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before 9/1/2019 or a more protective later ordinance.
rules.interaction: Does not apply where a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019 applies, or where a later local ordinance is more protective (with a binding local finding). A property cannot be subject to both. Less protective local ordinances adopted after September 1, 2019 are not enforced unless this section is repealed. Yields to r-0012 (Just cause required for eviction (Berkeley Rent Ordinance)): R9's interaction field says it does not apply where a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019 applies, and the Berkeley ordinance covers the same tenancies. Yields to r-0027 (Berkeley Just Cause for Eviction coverage): R9's interaction field says it does not apply to units covered by a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, and R8 sets Berkeley's coverage. Yields to r-0126 (San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction requirement): R9's exemptions field excludes property subject to a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before 9/1/2019, and R28 applies to units covered by the SF Rent Ordinance. Yields to r-0065 (RSO just cause eviction reasons): R9 does not apply where a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before 9/1/2019 applies, and R15 covers RSO units in Los Angeles. Yields to r-0060 (Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)): R9 yields to local ordinances in force on or before 9/1/2019, but R13's interaction field says AB 1482 may separately apply to JCO units. Yields to r-0119 (San Diego Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy): The San Diego ordinance (effective 2023) post-dates 9/1/2019, so under R9's interaction field it displaces the state rule only if it is more protective with a binding local finding, which the records do not show. Yields to r-0143 (Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance): The Santa Ana ordinance (effective 2021-11-19) post-dates 9/1/2019, so under R9's interaction field it governs only if it is more protective with a binding local finding, which the records do not show.
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.conflict_note: Uncertain whether r-0060 supersedes r-0036: R9 yields to local ordinances in force on or before 9/1/2019, but R13's interaction field says AB 1482 may separately apply to JCO units. Uncertain whether r-0119 supersedes r-0036: The San Diego ordinance (effective 2023) post-dates 9/1/2019, so under R9's interaction field it displaces the state rule only if it is more protective with a binding local finding, which the records do not show. Uncertain whether r-0143 supersedes r-0036: The Santa Ana ordinance (effective 2021-11-19) post-dates 9/1/2019, so under R9's interaction field it governs only if it is more protective with a binding local finding, which the records do not show. Conflict among r-0060, r-0036: R9 yields to local ordinances adopted on or before 9/1/2019, which would include the LA JCO, but R13 says AB 1482 may separately apply to JCO units. Review whether the state rule or the JCO governs just cause for non-RSO Los Angeles units. Conflict among r-0119, r-0036: San Diego's ordinance (effective 2023-06-24) post-dates 9/1/2019. R9 yields only if the local ordinance is more protective with a binding local finding. R24 says it is 'consistent with' § 1946.2, and the records do not show the finding. San Diego's 2 or 3 months of relocation also differs from the state's 1 month. Conflict among r-0143, r-0036: Santa Ana's ordinance (effective 2021-11-19) post-dates 9/1/2019. It applies after 30 days against the state's 12 months, and gives 3 months of relocation against the state's 1 month. Whether it is more protective with a binding local finding, so that R9 yields, is not shown.

rules.title: Relocation assistance or rent waiver for no-fault terminations
rules.requirement: When an owner terminates a covered tenancy for no-fault just cause, the owner must either pay relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent, and must state this right in the termination notice. Failure to strictly comply voids the notice.
rules.key_value: 1 month of rent (paid within 15 calendar days of service of the notice, or waived for the final month)

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenancies covered by the just cause requirement of § 1946.2 that are terminated for no-fault just cause, regardless of tenant income.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Same owner-based exemptions as the just cause requirement.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Applies only to no-fault terminations. A tenant found at fault for conditions triggering a government or court vacate order is not entitled to relocation assistance. The assistance is credited against any other relocation assistance required by other law.

rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as the just cause requirement; no relocation assistance where the tenant is at fault for conditions triggering a government or court vacate order.
rules.interaction: Credited against any other relocation assistance required by any other law. Yields to r-0120 (Relocation assistance for no-fault terminations): R11 has the same exemptions as the just cause requirement, which does not apply to a more protective later local ordinance, and R25's interaction field credits state assistance; whether R25 displaces R11 depends on the unsettled R24/R9 question. Yields to r-0144 (Santa Ana no-fault eviction relocation assistance): R11 follows R9's exemptions, which yield to a more protective later local ordinance, and R37 gives 3 months against R11's 1 month, but the binding local finding is not shown.
rules.quoted_span: The amount of relocation assistance or rent waiver shall be equal to one month of the tenant’s rent that was in effect when the owner issued the notice to terminate the tenancy.
rules.conflict_note: Uncertain whether r-0120 supersedes r-0037: R11 has the same exemptions as the just cause requirement, which does not apply to a more protective later local ordinance, and R25's interaction field credits state assistance; whether R25 displaces R11 depends on the unsettled R24/R9 question. Uncertain whether r-0144 supersedes r-0037: R11 follows R9's exemptions, which yield to a more protective later local ordinance, and R37 gives 3 months against R11's 1 month, but the binding local finding is not shown.

rules.title: Owner move-in termination conditions and tenant re-offer
rules.requirement: An owner-occupancy no-fault termination is valid only if the intended occupant moves in within 90 days after the tenant vacates and lives there as a primary residence for at least 12 consecutive months. Otherwise the owner must offer the unit back to the former tenant at the same rent and lease terms and reimburse reasonable moving expenses beyond any relocation assistance paid.
rules.key_value: 90 days to move in; 12 consecutive months of occupancy

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenancies covered by § 1946.2 terminated for owner or family member occupancy; for leases entered on or after July 1, 2020 (July 1, 2022 for mobilehomes), requires tenant written agreement or a lease provision allowing it.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Owner must be a natural person with at least a 25% recorded interest, or a qualifying related-owner group, or a natural person owning through an LLC or partnership. Not available if the intended occupant already occupies a unit on the property or a similar vacant unit exists.

rules.quoted_span: Clause (i) applies only if the intended occupant moves into the rental unit within 90 days after the tenant vacates and occupies the rental unit as a primary residence for at least 12 consecutive months.

rules.title: Statewide rent cap (Civ. Code § 1947.12, as amended by SB 567)
rules.requirement: An owner of residential real property may not, over any 12-month period, raise the gross rental rate by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, measured from the lowest gross rate charged in the prior 12 months. Where the same tenant remains in occupancy, no more than two increases are allowed in any 12-month period.
rules.key_value: lesser of 5% + CPI change or 10%; max two increases per 12 months

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential real property (including mobilehome park units) with a certificate of occupancy issued more than 15 years ago, other than exempt housing. Initial rent for a new tenancy is not capped. Does not apply to mobilehome homeowners.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Single-family homes and condos alienable separately from other units are exempt only if the owner is not a REIT, a corporation, an LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, and the tenant received the required written exemption notice. Owner-occupied duplexes are exempt.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Excludes deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing, dormitories, housing under stricter local rent control, and, as to the 15-year exemption, mobilehomes (which are not exempt). Does not apply to a homeowner of a mobilehome. New tenancies in which no prior tenant remains in possession may set their own initial rent.

rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; dormitories of higher education or K-12 schools; housing under stricter local rent or price control; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); separately alienable property (e.g., single-family homes, condos) not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, with written notice to tenants; a duplex where the owner occupies one unit as principal residence (neither unit an ADU or JADU); mobilehome homeowners.
rules.interaction: Does not expand or limit local governments' authority to adopt rent controls consistent with Chapter 2.7 (Civ. Code § 1954.50 et seq.). Housing under local rent control that restricts annual increases to less than the state cap is exempt. Does not authorize local limits not otherwise permitted by Chapter 2.7. Supersedes r-0062 (Statewide rent cap (AB 1482, California Tenant Protection Act of 2019)): R7 is the current statewide cap under Civ. Code § 1947.12 as amended by SB 567 (effective 2024-04-01), so it governs the original AB 1482 version in R8. Yields to r-0008 (Annual General Adjustment capped at 5% (Measure BB)): R7's exemptions and coverage_conditions exclude housing under stricter local rent control, and Berkeley's AGA cap of 5% is below the state cap of 5% plus CPI (up to 10%) for fully covered units. Yields to r-0025 (Berkeley 2026 Annual General Adjustment (Regulation 1148)): R7 exempts housing under stricter local rent control, and Berkeley's 2026 AGA of 1.0% is stricter than the state cap for eligible rent-stabilized units. Yields to r-0063 (Los Angeles RSO annual allowable rent increase): R7 exempts housing under stricter local rent control, and the LA RSO allowable increase applies to RSO-covered units. Yields to r-0067 (LA RSO annual allowable rent increase (3%, July 2025 to June 2026)): R7 exempts housing under stricter local rent control, and the LA RSO 3% allowable increase is below the state cap for RSO units. Yields to r-0128 (San Francisco annual allowable rent increase (3/1/2026–2/28/2027)): R7 exempts housing under stricter local rent control, and San Francisco's 1.6% allowable increase is stricter than the state cap for rent-controlled units. Yields to r-0132 (San Francisco allowable annual rent increase (Mar 2026 - Feb 2027)): R7 exempts housing under stricter local rent control, and San Francisco's 1.6% allowable increase is stricter than the state cap for covered units. Yields to r-0137 (Santa Ana annual maximum allowable rent increase): R7 exempts housing under stricter local rent control, and Santa Ana's cap of the lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI is stricter than the state cap. Yields to r-0141 (Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance annual cap): R7 exempts housing under stricter local rent control, and Santa Ana's cap of the lower of 3% or 80% of CPI applies to buildings built on or before 1995-02-01.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower

rules.title: Security deposit cap: one month's rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent, for residential rental property used as the tenant's dwelling. The cap applies to any payment, fee, deposit or charge however denominated.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential rental property used as the tenant's dwelling; applies to security collected or demanded on or after July 1, 2024.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024.

rules.exemptions: Advance payment of not less than six months' rent when the lease term is six months or longer; agreed fee for tenant-requested alterations; small-landlord two-month rule in paragraph (5).
rules.interaction: Yields to r-0041 (Small-landlord security cap: two months' rent): R11's interaction field says it operates as an exception to the one-month cap in paragraph (1), and R13's exemptions list the small-landlord two-month rule in paragraph (5), so R11 governs for qualifying small landlords.
rules.quoted_span: Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.

rules.title: Small-landlord security cap: two months' rent
rules.requirement: A landlord who is a natural person or an all-natural-person LLC and owns no more than two rental properties with no more than four units in total may not demand or receive security above two months' rent. This higher cap does not apply when the prospective tenant is a service member, and the landlord may not refuse to rent to a service member because of it.
rules.key_value: 2 months' rent (small landlords)

coverage_conditions.summary: Small landlords only: natural persons or LLCs whose members are all natural persons, owning no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four dwelling units offered for rent in total.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Landlord is a natural person (including a settlor or beneficiary of a family trust) or an LLC in which all members are natural persons, and owns no more than two residential rental properties collectively including no more than four dwelling units offered for rent.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Not applicable if the prospective tenant is a service member; the one-month cap in paragraph (1) then applies.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply when the prospective tenant is a service member.
rules.interaction: Operates as an exception to the one-month cap in paragraph (1). Supersedes r-0040 (Security deposit cap: one month's rent): R11's interaction field says it operates as an exception to the one-month cap in paragraph (1), and R13's exemptions list the small-landlord two-month rule in paragraph (5), so R11 governs for qualifying small landlords.
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to two months’ rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy if the landlord meets both of the following requirements:
rules.conflict_note: Conflict among r-0018, r-0041: R6 says a small landlord may charge up to two months' rent and does not mention R11's service-member exception, where the one-month cap applies. R6's interaction field also says the Berkeley Rent Board cannot determine whether a landlord may charge one or two months' rent for a new tenancy. A reviewer should confirm the service-member carve-out applies and how the cap is applied in Berkeley.

rules.title: Higher security for service members: written explanation and return after six months
rules.requirement: If a landlord charges a service member higher than standard or advertised security because of credit history, credit score, housing history or similar factors, the landlord must give a written statement of the amount and the reason on or before lease signing. The additional amount must be returned after no more than six months of residency if the tenant is not in arrears.
rules.key_value: Return of additional security after no more than 6 months

coverage_conditions.summary: Service members renting residential property in which they will reside, where the landlord charges higher than standard or advertised security.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Tenant must be a service member as defined in Military and Veterans Code § 400; return of the additional amount requires the tenant not to be in arrears.

rules.quoted_span: if a landlord or its agent charges a service member who rents residential property in which the service member will reside a higher than standard or advertised security pursuant to paragraph (1) due to the credit history, credit score, housing history, or other factor related to the tenant, the landlord shall provide the tenant with a written statement, on or before the date the lease is signed, of the amount of the higher security and an explanation why the higher security amount is being charged.

rules.title: Limits on deductions from security (no ordinary wear and tear)
rules.requirement: A landlord may deduct only amounts reasonably necessary for default in rent, repair of tenant-caused damage, necessary cleaning and similar purposes. The landlord may not charge for preexisting damage or ordinary wear and tear, and may not charge for professional cleaning unless reasonably necessary to restore the unit to its condition at the start of the tenancy.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential rental property used as the tenant's dwelling.

rules.quoted_span: The landlord shall not assert a claim against the tenant or the security for damages to the premises or any defective conditions that preexisted the tenancy, for ordinary wear and tear or the effects thereof, whether the wear and tear preexisted the tenancy or occurred during the tenancy, or for the cumulative effects of ordinary wear and tear occurring during any one or more tenancies.

rules.title: Security deposit return and itemized statement within 21 days
rules.requirement: Within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, the landlord must furnish an itemized statement of the basis for and amount of any security received and its disposition, and return any remaining portion. Return must be electronic if the landlord received security or rent electronically, and by check to all adult tenants when several reside in the unit, unless otherwise agreed in writing.
rules.key_value: 21 calendar days

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential rental property used as the tenant's dwelling.

rules.quoted_span: the landlord shall furnish the tenant, a copy of an itemized statement indicating the basis for, and the amount of, any security received and the disposition of the security, and shall return any remaining portion of the security to the tenant as follows:

rules.title: Documentation of repair and cleaning deductions
rules.requirement: The landlord must send copies of bills, invoices or receipts, or a description of work done by the landlord with time and hourly rate, along with the itemized statement, plus photographs. A good-faith estimate is allowed if work cannot be completed within 21 days. Documentation is not required if total repair and cleaning deductions do not exceed $125 or the tenant validly waived it, unless the tenant requests it within 14 days.
rules.key_value: $125 documentation threshold

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential rental property used as the tenant's dwelling.

rules.exemptions: Deductions for repairs and cleaning not exceeding $125 in total; valid tenant waiver (subject to the tenant's right to request documentation within 14 days).
rules.quoted_span: If the landlord or landlord’s employee did not do the work, the landlord shall provide the tenant a copy of the bill, invoice, or receipt supplied by the person or entity performing the work.

rules.title: Landlord photographs of the unit
rules.requirement: Landlords must photograph the unit at the start of tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025. Beginning April 1, 2025, they must photograph the unit after possession is returned but before deduction-related repairs or cleanings, and again after those are completed.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential rental property used as the tenant's dwelling; move-in photographs required for tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Move-in photographs apply to tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025; move-out photographs apply from April 1, 2025.

rules.quoted_span: Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord, but prior to any repairs or cleanings for which the landlord will make a deduction from or claim against the security deposit pursuant to this section, and shall also take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after such repairs or cleanings are completed.

rules.title: Initial inspection and itemized statement of proposed deductions
rules.requirement: On the tenant's request, the landlord must conduct an initial inspection before move-out and give the tenant an itemized statement of proposed deductions. The tenant may then remedy the deficiencies, and the landlord generally cannot deduct for items not identified in the statement.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential rental property used as the tenant's dwelling.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply when the tenancy is terminated under CCP § 1161(2), (3) or (4).
rules.quoted_span: Based on the inspection, the landlord shall give the tenant an itemized statement specifying repairs or cleanings that are proposed to be the basis of any deductions from the security the landlord intends to make pursuant to paragraphs (1) to (4), inclusive, of subdivision (b).

rules.title: Ban on 'nonrefundable' security provisions
rules.requirement: A lease or rental agreement may not characterize any security as nonrefundable.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential rental agreements for property used as the tenant's dwelling.

rules.quoted_span: A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”

rules.title: Bad-faith retention of security: statutory damages
rules.requirement: A landlord or successor who in bad faith claims or retains security in violation of the section may owe statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages. The landlord bears the burden of proving the reasonableness of the amounts claimed.
rules.key_value: up to 2x the security amount

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential rental property used as the tenant's dwelling.

rules.quoted_span: The bad faith claim or retention by a landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest of the security or any portion thereof in violation of this section, or the bad faith demand of replacement of security in violation of subdivision (k), may subject the landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.

rules.title: Application screening fee cap (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee only to cover actual out-of-pocket costs of gathering information on the applicant and the reasonable value of time spent, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjustable annually for CPI increases since January 1, 1998).
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted annually

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to landlords (owners of residential rental property) and their agents charging applicants, including guarantors and cosigners, for residential rental units.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Does not preempt provisions governing collection of deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.

rules.interaction: Applies notwithstanding Section 1950.5; the fee is not 'security' under 1950.5. Does not preempt federal or state housing assistance program rules on deposits and fees.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
rules.conflict_note: Conflict among r-0007, r-0050: Both describe the Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6 screening fee cap but state different figures: R3 gives a 2026 maximum of $68.96, while R6 gives $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted annually. These are probably consistent, since $68.96 would be the CPI-adjusted 2026 amount of the $30 base. A reviewer should confirm this and treat them as one rule from two sources rather than two caps.

rules.title: No screening fee when no unit available
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not charge an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available or will be available within a reasonable period of time.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to landlords and agents charging applicants for residential rental units.

rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause stated in a written notice. At-fault causes include nonpayment, material lease breach, nuisance and criminal activity; no-fault causes include owner occupancy, withdrawal from the rental market, and demolition or substantial remodel. Owners must first give notice of a violation with time to cure before a for-cause termination.

rules.title: Prohibition against algorithmic rent-fixing (Hoboken)
rules.requirement: Landlords renting any residential dwelling unit in Hoboken may not use software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms that collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information to coordinate, recommend or implement rental prices, lease terms or occupancy levels among competing lessors. Violations are enforceable in Hoboken Municipal Court by the Division of Housing or an aggrieved private citizen, with penalties of a fine up to $2,000, up to 90 days of community service, or penalties under N.J.S.A. 40:49-5.

coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Residential dwelling unit means any primary residence, excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities. Nonpublic competitor information is information less than 365 days old that is not widely and readily available to the public at no cost.

rules.exemptions: Medical/long-term care facilities and detention facilities are excluded from the definition of residential dwelling unit.
